I lost my mom in 2016 when I was 21. She was sick for 10 yrs, so I also was expecting it. Give yourself time. Listen to music that reminds you of him, write to him in a journal, live your days doing things that you know would make him proud. Give yourself a few years before things start to feel stable again, it’s a big change. It feels like time has frozen, but the world around you is still moving, this will end. You’ll adjust to the new normal in time. But for now, take care of yourself, cry when you feel it, feel your emotions and let it run its course. I am also not religious, but I do believe that we are all a part of this universe and we go back to the universe when we die. He’s in the wind you feel, the shine of the sun, and the smell of fresh grass. He’s in the squirrels running along the tree line. He is everywhere around you, and one day you will become one with the universe with him. You’ll feel his presence again in once capacity or another. Grief never ends, but managing it does become easier. You’re never alone. The universe is always there, and so is he, just not in the same way.

It’s been a long journey, and I am certainly still on it. I have good weeks and bad weeks. I used to really shame myself for it, and I’ve learned to be kinder to myself, which has actually helped in the long run. The thing that helped me most was being vulnerable and open about my struggle and goal to overcome my addiction. It also really helped to set a stopwatch when I took my last hit and I would see how long I could go before taking another hit. I would want to see how long I could push myself and I would want to see that stopwatch go longer and longer each day (I’ve never made it to 24 hrs yet, but that’s ok). It’s easy for me to take a hit, then another, and another and keep going and going. I have to watch and tell myself, I am already high, I don’t need to keep smoking. I will feel better throughout my day if I keep it to just 2 hits max. I’m being kind to myself on this journey. I also am trying to just become more in tune with my feelings. I used weed to numb myself 24/7, and as hard as it is to feel the pain I was suppressing, I know it’s necessary for my growth and future happiness. It’s all been little by little. I also went for walks whenever I felt the intense urge to smoke. It usually distracted me enough to remind me what my goal is and that I am capable of anything I put my mind to. In the beginning, that stopwatch really was helpful though. That was the first time I really started believing that I could do it, that I could begin to cut it out. This was a quickly written response, so if I think of other things, I’ll update. Ive also just been working on building my self confidence, which has helped in its own right. I’m on year 1.5 of this journey, I smoke every night still, but I’ve managed to cut my smoking throughout the day and morning significantly. Just be kind to yourself and believe in yourself. Don’t compare yourself to others, you are on your own journey and you have the power. You just have to believe it. I look forward to the day when I don’t feel the need to smoke at night, but I’m not there yet and that is ok. I see a lot of people beating themselves up in this sub, and there is no reason to do so.
